title: The Thousand Years and the Great White Throne

verses.text: Then I saw an angel coming down from heaven with the key to the Abyss, holding in his hand a great chain.
He seized the dragon, that ancient serpent who is the devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years.

And he threw him into the Abyss, shut it, and sealed it over him, so that he could not deceive the nations until the thousand years were complete. After that, he must be released for a brief period of time.

Then I saw the thrones, and those seated on them had been given authority to judge. And I saw the souls of those who had been beheaded for their testimony of Jesus and for the word of God, and those who had not worshiped the beast or its image, and had not received its mark on their foreheads or hands. And they came to life and reigned with Christ for a thousand years.
The rest of the dead did not come back to life until the thousand years were complete. This is the first resurrection.
Blessed and holy are those who share in the first resurrection! The second death has no power over them, but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and will reign with Him for a thousand years.
When the thousand years are complete, Satan will be released from his prison,
and will go out to deceive the nations in the four corners of the earth—Gog and Magog—to assemble them for battle. Their number is like the sand of the seashore.
And they marched across the broad expanse of the earth and surrounded the camp of the saints and the beloved city. But fire came down from heaven and consumed them.

And the devil who had deceived them was thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur, into which the beast and the false prophet had already been thrown. There they will be tormented day and night forever and ever.
Then I saw a great white throne and the One seated on it. Earth and heaven fled from His presence, and no place was found for them.

And I saw the dead, great and small, standing before the throne. And there were open books, and one of them was the Book of Life. And the dead were judged according to their deeds, as recorded in the books.
The sea gave up its dead, and Death and Hades gave up their dead, and each one was judged according to his deeds.
Then Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death—the lake of fire.
And if anyone was found whose name was not written in the Book of Life, he was thrown into the lake of fire.

context.author: John, who was on the island of Patmos (1:1, 4, 9); traditionally the apostle John
context.genre: Apocalypse, prophecy, and letter, full of symbols and visions
context.audience: Seven churches in the Roman province of Asia
context.setting: An angel binds the dragon for a thousand years and throws him into the abyss. Those who were beheaded for their testimony come to life and reign with Christ for a thousand years. When the thousand years are over, Satan is released and gathers Gog and Magog for battle, but fire from heaven consumes them. Then John sees the great white throne, and the dead are judged by their works.
context.custom: This passage is one of the most discussed in Scripture and gives rise to three main readings: premillennial (Christ returns before the thousand years), postmillennial (after), and amillennial (the thousand years is symbolic of the present age). Believers have disagreed on this since the early church.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 21 describes the new heaven and new earth.
context.timelineBible: Gog and Magog come from Ezekiel 38-39. The great white throne recalls Daniel 7:9-10, and the books opened echo Daniel 7:10 and 12:1.

translation.meaning: A long period. The Latin “millennium” comes from it.

otBackground.note: The Ancient of Days and the books opened.

overview.summary: Satan is bound, and the saints reign with Christ for a thousand years. After a final rebellion, the dead are judged at the great white throne, and death itself is destroyed.
overview.settingLine: Satan bound, then the final judgment.

history.t: Pre-, post-, and amillennial views each appear in church history.
Symbolic of hostile nations in Jewish tradition.

archaeology.t: A text about the final battle.
Judges sat on a raised platform.
From medieval church doorways to Michelangelo’s Sistine Chapel, the great white throne of 20:11-15 became one of the most painted scenes in Christian art.

overview.discussion: There are different views on the thousand years. How can I hold my view humbly and still be gracious to Christians who differ?
overview.book: The book of Revelation · 22 chapters. A vision of Christ, judgment, and the new creation, written to encourage persecuted believers.
overview.author: John

historicalImage.caption: The Angel with the Key to the Bottomless Pit, from Dürer’s Apocalypse: the angel locks the dragon in the Abyss, while another angel shows John the new Jerusalem (Revelation 20:1-3; 21:9-10).
historicalImage.credit: Albrecht Dürer (1498), National Gallery of Art, Washington, CC0 / Wikimedia Commons

currentImage.caption: The Last Judgment by Michelangelo, painted on the altar wall of the Sistine Chapel in 1536-1541. Christ judges the dead, who rise from the earth, a picture of the great white throne of Revelation 20:11-15.
